From: security@kestrel.com (Katie Ruiz)

Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SBOM + pen test summary + VM cadence for vendor assessment

Hi Monica,

We are running a vendor security assessment for Redwood as part of Kestrel Finance's procurement for our payments platform. Could you provide the following artifacts and clarifications by EOD Aug 5 (PDT)?

- Third-party OSS inventory / SBOM (preferred CycloneDX or SPDX; PURLs if possible) covering the inference runtime and model-serving components.
- Recent pen test summary (executive findings) and scope (external/internal).
- SAST/DAST tooling names, scan cadence, and how findings feed into your vuln triage.
- Patch remediation SLAs by severity (CVE remediation targets).
- If any libraries or dependencies are redacted for IP reasons, a brief explanation and an alternative evidence plan.

We may redact some items in our report — if you need an NDA addendum or a redaction process, let us know. If helpful, copy your pen-test vendor to coordinate.

Thanks,
Katie Ruiz
Security Program Manager
Kestrel Finance

Monica / Aditya —

Quick status and what I attached to this thread:
- redwood_sbom_thirdparty_2025-07-30.csv (CycloneDX-like CSV export we generate from our build pipeline; includes PURLs for third-party packages used in the serving runtime).
- vm_patch_sla_matrix.xlsx (internal SLA table: Critical = 48 hours to mitigation plan / 7 days to patch; High = 7 days; Medium = 30 days; Low = 90 days) — note these are our customer-facing targets for hosted and dedicated customers; Private deployments can agree custom SLAs in contracts.
- pen_test_summary_magma_2025-07.pdf (executive summary from MagmaSec pen test on 2025-07-15; scope = external network + application layer including API endpoints and model-serving control plane). Full report is vendor-controlled; we can provide the exec summary and remediation plan.

Notes:
- SAST: we run Semgrep + custom rules in CI for our monorepo; gate on main branch and weekly scheduled scans for infra libs. Findings are triaged via our ticketing flow (SEC-XXXX) and assigned severities mapped to the SLA matrix above.
- DAST: ZAP-based scans on staging every night for public endpoints; scheduled authenticated scans weekly for admin APIs. Findings automatically create Jira tickets with run artifacts attached.
- SBOM: generated at build time for the runtime artifact and the packaging layer. We include license and checksum fields. For model binaries that include third-party libs from model vendors, we provide a hashed SBOM (component names redacted, sha256 hashes included); vendor contracts sometimes restrict full disclosure.
- Remediation evidence: for critical findings we provide a ticket, commit reference, and patch note; we can pull a redacted timeline for Kestrel if they need audit trace evidence.

I attached the three files named above to my reply. If Kestrel prefers SPDX or CycloneDX JSON, we can export that — CSV is the quickest.

-Priyom
Priyom Das
Security Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Adding a few runtime and operational points Kestrel typically asks about — feel free to copy into the customer email:

- Runtime hardening: inference runtime runs in sandboxed containers with seccomp + AppArmor profiles; GPU drivers pinned per image to a fixed vendor hash.
- Model dependencies: third-party inference kernels and quantization helpers are pinned and updated as part of our weekly dependency window; we publish a rolling CVE dashboard in the Console that surfaces high/critical CVEs affecting the runtime. Customers on Dedicated get push notifications.
- Pen test scope clarification: MagmaSec did an external blackbox + authenticated API layer test; we engaged them to validate CVE remediation verification for the highest severity items after our patch. The attached exec summary includes the verification notes.

I also attached the pen test executive summary from MagmaSec (redacted for customer PII).

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
VP, Infrastructure and Reliability

Katie —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find the attachments we can share today: redwood_sbom_thirdparty_2025-07-30.csv (CycloneDX-style CSV), pen_test_summary_magma_2025-07.pdf (exec summary, scope & verification notes), and vm_patch_sla_matrix.xlsx (target remediation SLAs).

What these include:
- SBOM: runtime and packaging layers with PURLs and checksums. For model vendor-supplied binaries we provide hashed SBOM entries and the rationale for redaction (contractual restrictions). If Kestrel needs full disclosure we can escalate to legal for an NDA addendum.
- Pen test: MagmaSec performed an external + authenticated API assessment on 2025-07-15. Executive findings and verification notes are in the attached PDF. Full vendor report is available under an NDA and can be provided through MagmaSec.
- SAST/DAST cadence and triage: semgrep + scheduled DAST runs; findings create Jira tickets with remediation owners and SLA tracking.
- Patch SLAs (summary): Critical = mitigation plan within 48 hours, hotpatch/mitigation within 7 days; High = 7 days; Medium = 30 days; Low = 90 days. We included the full matrix in the XLS. Private deployment customers can negotiate different timelines in their contract.

Links & next steps:
- Shared evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-vm-evidence
- Tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4821 (public-redacted view)
